subject: [Escalation] Production p99 spike + 429 feedback loop impacting checkout - ACME
messages:
From: Aaron Diaz <aaron.diaz@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts impacting checkout

Rachel —

We started seeing large p95/p99 spikes on the Hosted API around 14:58 UTC this morning. Our checkout path that calls your /v1/generate endpoint is intermittently hitting 500s and 429s; customers are seeing timeouts and abandoned carts. High-level: request volume hasn't changed on our end, but our client retrier kicked up after seeing 429s which made spikes worse.

Attached are snippets from our client-side logs showing the retry pattern and timestamps. This is urgent — we are seeing user impact on production. Can Redwood either temporarily raise our quota, route traffic differently, or advise an immediate mitigation?

Aaron Diaz
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 15:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts impacting checkout

Aaron —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I'm escalating this to our SRE and CS teams — looping in Marcus, Priyom, and Tessa. We're treating this as an incident (impacting production checkout).

Quick asks while we triage:
- Can you confirm approximate QPS for the checkout call and whether you recently flipped any client-side retry/backoff config?
- If you can share a single request id from a failed request, we can correlate on our side.

Immediate mitigation options we can try (please indicate which you'd like us to push):
1) Temporary quota bump for the next 2 hours to reduce 429 issuance (manual override).
2) Route ACME traffic to a reserved pool (if you have Dedicated capacity) or to a different region for short-term relief.
3) Server-side throttling policy change: increase per-customer token bucket and enable stricter tail-timeout guarding (drops long-running requests earlier).

We will surface a short incident summary and suggested next steps in the next 30–45 minutes.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mailto:rachel_kim@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts impacting checkout

Rachel / team —

Initial findings from the runtime: we see a classic 429->client-retry feedback loop originating at ~14:55 UTC. The Hosted API's recent conservative global rate-limit bump (applied at 14:30 UTC for a separate account surge) tightened per-customer limits for some customers unexpectedly due to a policy propagation bug. ACME hit that tighter window and their clients started aggressive retrying (short backoff), which amplified queue depth and pushed token processing into slower CPU fallback paths — that explains the p95/p99 regressions and increased timeouts.

What I recommend right now (order matters):
- Immediate: roll back the propagation change to the previous per-customer limit profile (we can do a hotfix rollback now).
- Immediate: enable per-tenant circuit-breaker (5xx/429 threshold) that will reject quickly without queuing to prevent long-tail amplification.
- Short term: raise ACME's manual concurrency quota by 3x for 60 minutes to drain backlog.
- Medium term: add jittered exponential backoff guidance to our SDK and set default client retry to conservative values in our sample code.

I'm attaching the SLO dashboard snapshot and a filtered runtime log slice around the window.

—Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo-dashboard-20260309.png (image), ingest-logs-20260309.zip (logs)
From: Aaron Diaz <aaron.diaz@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts impacting checkout

Thanks — we did increase aggressive retries on our side earlier this morning after seeing intermittent 429s (client default). We'll revert to conservative retries if you can confirm a short window where you will either increase quota or roll traffic.

Our timeline: first 429 at 14:55:32 UTC, then client retrier attempted 3 fast retries at 14:55:32–14:55:36 which coincides with the spike in your p99.

If rolling back the rate-limit profile and a temporary quota increase (or routing to reserved capacity) will stop the retries from spiraling, that will be fine. We prefer not to fail open for long (we need a temporary engineered solution + follow-up).

Aaron
